Firm size and return on penny stocks : The signiﬁcance of t-test results suggests that within a sample of
penny stocks listed in the Indian stock market, there exists a negative association between ﬁrm size and average
returns (as indicated by the correlation also). We report that the top 50 percent of penny stocks, sorted on the
basis of size as denoted by market capitalization, have generated lower returns compared to the stocks from the
bottom 50 percent. It implies that smaller is the ﬁrm size, higher is the average returns. This seems very much
aligned with the classical theory that suggests smaller ﬁrms have more information asymmetry and carry higher
risk, hence the expected return must be higher when compared to bigger ﬁrms. The empirical model such as
Fama-French three factor model also states the same. Our simple comparison of average returns support the
hypothesis.
uWe show that beta is positively correlated with the ﬁrm size (market cap) which is counter-intuitive as it

higher for the smaller ﬁrms but only sees volatility and thus our paper points to the failure of beta to measure
risk fully. The size eﬀect is not due to the so called risk measured by beta. There is some other cause on why
lower market cap penny stocks earn higher returns. It appears that the fundamental risk or asymmetry not
16

fully captured by the beta. Essentially then, a portfolio of low market cap penny stocks have higher returns as
well as low volatility which is great from investors point of view. Also, this reverse trend can explain why beta
is not statistically signiﬁcant in t-test despite being correlated with returns.
P/E ratio and P/B ratio : A statistically signiﬁcant t-statistic suggest that the returns on stocks belonging
to bottom 50 percent when sorted on their P/E ratios are substantially higher than the returns on penny stocks
from the top 50 percent of the P/E ratio-sorted stock group. A similar behavior is observed when we sorted
the stocks on the basis of P/B ratio and test for the diﬀerences in means of returns on top 50 percent stocks
and bottom 50 percent stocks. These two functions, namely, P/E and P/B ratios are established risk factors
validated both theoretically and empirically across the markets and our results support the hypotheses laid out
earlier.
The t-test results obtained for shareholding pattern, beta, and liquidity do not yield favorable results,
suggesting that the returns on top 50 percent penny stocks are statistically and signiﬁcantly indiﬀerent from
the returns on bottom 50 percent penny stocks when sorted on the basis or these functions. It appears that
since most of the penny stocks belong to the ﬁrms held largely by the families and small business operators,
shareholding pattern turns out to be an insigniﬁcant diﬀerentiator of returns on such stocks. Similarly, stocks
when sorted on the basis of beta do not exhibit diﬀerent pattern across top and bottom 50 percentiles. Liquidity
factor is another redundant input as the sample penny stocks are very illiquid and rarely traded. It comes as
no surprise to us as liquidity can inﬂuence returns only when it is heavily traded, resulting into high trading
volume and price ﬂuctuations.

starting with early/top 50 percent of alphabets (such as A, B, C, ..., L, M) have shown better average returns

number of alternatives, each with diﬀerent risk and return characteristics, any economic agent tends to satisﬁce,
whereby search ceases after an economically acceptable option is found, even if a better option could be found

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""

        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import decay_linear, rank, ts_sum, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_LEVY_WIN = 60      # bars in the rolling signature window
_VOL_WIN = 60       # bars for volatility / volume normalisation
_DRIFT_WIN = 6      # bars of peer drift that gets pushed onto the follower
_MIN_FRAC = 0.6     # fraction of the window that must be valid


def _static_groups(sector: object, columns: pd.Index) -> pd.Series:
    """Map every ticker to a static sector label using its EARLIEST observed
    label (point-in-time safe: never uses a label stamped after t for a name
    that already had one, and sector membership is a static attribute)."""
    labels: dict[object, str] = {}
    if isinstance(sector, pd.DataFrame):
        for c in columns:
            lab = "UNKNOWN"
            if c in sector.columns:
                col = sector[c]
                if isinstance(col, pd.DataFrame):
                    col = col.iloc[:, 0]
                col = col.dropna()
                if len(col) > 0:
                    lab = str(col.iloc[0])
            labels[c] = lab
    else:
        for c in columns:
            labels[c] = "UNKNOWN"
    return pd.Series(labels, index=pd.Index(columns), dtype=object)


def _ex_self_group_mean(df: pd.DataFrame, groups: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Per-row, per-sector mean EXCLUDING the name itself (NaN-aware)."""
    vals = df.astype(float)
    mask = vals.notna()
    filled = vals.fillna(0.0)
    out = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=df.index, columns=df.columns, dtype=float)
    for lab in pd.unique(groups.values):
        cols = [c for c in groups.index[groups.values == lab] if c in df.columns]
        if len(cols) < 2:
            continue
        tot = filled[cols].sum(axis=1)
        cnt = mask[cols].astype(float).sum(axis=1)
        num = (-filled[cols]).add(tot, axis=0)
        den = (-mask[cols].astype(float)).add(cnt, axis=0)
        den = den.where(den > 0.0)
        out[cols] = num / den
    return out


def _group_demean(df: pd.DataFrame, groups: pd.Series) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Subtract the per-row sector mean (cross-sectional, no look-ahead)."""
    out = df.astype(float).copy()
    for lab in pd.unique(groups.values):
        cols = [c for c in groups.index[groups.values == lab] if c in df.columns]
        if len(cols) == 0:
            continue
        sub = out[cols]
        out[cols] = sub.sub(sub.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    return out


def _rolling_levy_area(dx: pd.DataFrame, dy: pd.DataFrame, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Discrete Lévy area (level-2 antisymmetric signature term) of the two
    channel path (X, Y) built from increments dx, dy over the trailing n bars:

        A_t = 1/2 * sum_{j=t-n+1}^{t} ( X_{j-1} dY_j - Y_{j-1} dX_j )

    with X, Y measured relative to the start of the window (so the object is
    translation invariant).  Written with global cumulative sums plus positive
    shifts, hence O(1) per bar and strictly causal: the value at t only ever
    touches increments dated <= t.  A_t > 0 means X leads Y; A_t < 0 means X
    lags (follows) Y.
    """
    x = dx.fillna(0.0)
    y = dy.fillna(0.0)
    cx = x.cumsum()
    cy = y.cumsum()
    cx_lag = cx.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
    cy_lag = cy.shift(1).fillna(0.0)
    p = (cx_lag * y).cumsum()          # running sum of X_{j-1} dY_j
    q = (cy_lag * x).cumsum()          # running sum of Y_{j-1} dX_j

    cx0 = cx.shift(n)                  # cumulative level just before window
    cy0 = cy.shift(n)
    p0 = p.shift(n)
    q0 = q.shift(n)

    term_xy = (p - p0) - cx0 * (cy - cy0)
    term_yx = (q - q0) - cy0 * (cx - cx0)
    return 0.5 * (term_xy - term_yx)


@register_factor
class LevyAreaFollowerRankUntradedSpillover(BaseFactor):
    """Push the sector composite's fresh drift onto Lévy-area followers whose own
    tape is still asleep while peer volume surges."""

    factor_id = "levy_area_follower_rank_untraded_spillover"
    name = "Lévy-Area Follower Score × Untraded-Tape Peer Spillover"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "For each name, compute the discrete Lévy area between its "
        "volatility-scaled cumulative return path and its sector peers' "
        "(ex-self) composite path over a rolling window, normalised to a "
        "bounded lead(+)/lag(-) leadership score; take the follower part of "
        "that score, multiply it by the peers' recent volatility-scaled drift "
        "and by a gate measuring peer-volume surge minus own-volume surge, "
        "then demean/rank cross-sectionally within sector."
    )
    window_length = 180
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float)
        groups = _static_groups(data.get("sector"), close.columns)

        # ---- volatility-scaled own return increments -----------------------
        px = close.where(close > 0.0)
        ret = np.log(px).diff()
        sigma = ret.rolling(_VOL_WIN, min_periods=max(10, _VOL_WIN // 3)).std()
        sigma = sigma.replace(0.0, np.nan)
        dx = (ret / sigma).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        # ---- ex-self sector composite path increments ----------------------
        dy = _ex_self_group_mean(dx, groups).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        # ---- level-2 signature: Lévy area own-path vs peer-composite path --
        area = _rolling_levy_area(dx, dy, _LEVY_WIN)

        # bounded leadership score in [-1, 1]: |A| <= 1/2 * L1(X) * L1(Y)
        lx = ts_sum(dx.abs().fillna(0.0), _LEVY_WIN)
        ly = ts_sum(dy.abs().fillna(0.0), _LEVY_WIN)
        norm = (0.5 * lx * ly).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        lead = (area / norm).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

        # only trust the score where the window is mostly populated
        valid = (dx.notna() & dy.notna()).astype(float)
        enough = valid.rolling(_LEVY_WIN, min_periods=1).sum() >= (_MIN_FRAC * _LEVY_WIN)
        lead = lead.where(enough)

        # follower part of the leadership score: negative Lévy area only
        follower = (-lead).clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- peers' fresh volatility-scaled drift --------------------------
        peer_drift = np.tanh(decay_linear(dy.fillna(0.0), _DRIFT_WIN))

        # ---- untraded-tape gate: peer volume surge minus own volume surge --
        lv = np.log1p(volume.fillna(0.0).clip(lower=0.0))
        own_surge = ts_zscore(lv, _VOL_WIN).clip(-6.0, 6.0)
        peer_surge = _ex_self_group_mean(own_surge, groups)
        asym = (peer_surge - own_surge)
        gate = np.tanh(0.5 * asym.fillna(0.0)).clip(lower=0.0)

        # ---- combine, sector-demean, cross-sectional rank ------------------
        raw = follower * peer_drift * gate
        raw = raw.where(dy.notna())
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        demeaned = _group_demean(raw.fillna(0.0), groups)
        demeaned = demeaned.where(raw.notna())

        out = rank(demeaned) - 0.5
        out = out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return out.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (

        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import adv, rolling_autocorr, rolling_beta
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_SQ = 1.0 / np.sqrt(2.0)


def _uwp_packets(x: pd.DataFrame, levels: int = 3) -> list[pd.DataFrame]:
    """Causal undecimated (a-trous) Haar wavelet-packet transform.

    Node ordering is 'natural': index 0 is the all-lowpass (trend) packet.
    Every output at t is a fixed FIR combination of x[t], x[t-1], ... only,
    so the transform is strictly causal (no decimation, no centering).
    """
    nodes = [x]
    for lev in range(levels):
        dil = 1 << lev                       # dilation 1, 2, 4, ...
        nxt: list[pd.DataFrame] = []
        for node in nodes:
            prev = node.shift(dil)
            nxt.append((node + prev) * _SQ)  # lowpass half-band
            nxt.append((node - prev) * _SQ)  # highpass half-band
        nodes = nxt
    return nodes


def _resonator_state(y: pd.DataFrame, n: int):
    """Trailing damped-sinusoid (AR(2) resonator) fit of a band signal.

    Uses r_1 = rho*cos(w), r_2 = rho^2*cos(2w)  =>  cos^2(w) = r1^2/(2r1^2-r2).
    Returns (energy, omega, rho, narrowbandness) as DataFrames.  All inputs are
    trailing rolling statistics, hence causal.
    """
    mp = max(8, n // 2)
    energy = (y * y).rolling(n, min_periods=mp).mean()

    r1 = rolling_autocorr(y, n, 1)
    r2 = rolling_autocorr(y, n, 2)
    r1c = r1.clip(-0.98, 0.98)
    r2c = r2.clip(-0.98, 0.98)

    denom = 2.0 * (r1c ** 2) - r2c
    c2 = (r1c ** 2) / denom.where(denom.abs() > 1e-4)
    ok = (denom > 1e-4) & (c2 > 1e-4) & (c2 <= 1.0)

    c_fit = np.sign(r1c) * np.sqrt(c2.clip(1e-4, 1.0))
    cos_w = c_fit.where(ok, r1c)             # fallback: rho == 1 (pure tone)
    cos_w = cos_w.clip(-0.995, 0.995)

    omega = np.arccos(cos_w).clip(0.15, 3.0)
    rho = (r1c / cos_w.replace(0.0, np.nan)).clip(0.05, 0.99)
    rho = rho.fillna(0.5)

    q = -omega / (2.0 * np.log(rho))         # resonator quality factor
    q = q.clip(0.0, 40.0)
    narrow = q / (1.0 + q)
    return energy, omega, rho, narrow


def _quadrature(y: pd.DataFrame, omega: pd.DataFrame):
    """Causal quadrature companion of a narrowband signal."""
    sw = np.sin(omega)
    sw = sw.where(sw.abs() > 1e-2)
    s = (y * np.cos(omega) - y.shift(1)) / sw
    return s


def _extrap_kernel(rho: np.ndarray, omega: np.ndarray, h: int) -> np.ndarray:
    """sum_{k=1..h} z^k with z = rho*exp(i*omega) (damped harmonic forecast)."""
    z = rho * np.exp(1j * omega)
    one_minus = 1.0 - z
    with np.errstate(divide="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
        ker = z * (1.0 - z ** h) / one_minus
    bad = ~np.isfinite(ker.real) | ~np.isfinite(ker.imag) | (np.abs(one_minus) < 1e-3)
    ker = np.where(bad, np.nan + 0j, ker)
    return ker

from __future__ import annotations

import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import stats

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _rank1d(x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Cross-sectional percentile rank in (0, 1); non-finite entries -> 0.5."""
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    out = np.full(x.shape, 0.5, dtype=float)
    good = np.isfinite(x)
    n = int(good.sum())
    if n >= 2:
        r = stats.rankdata(x[good])
        out[good] = (r - 0.5) / float(n)
    return out


def _onnela_clustering(W: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Onnela weighted local clustering coefficient of a non-negative,
    zero-diagonal, max-normalised weight matrix W.

        C_i = sum_{j,k} (w_ij w_jk w_ki)^(1/3) / (d_i (d_i - 1))

    which equals diag(A^3)_i / (d_i (d_i - 1)) with A = W ** (1/3) and d_i the
    number of non-zero links of i.
    """
    A = np.cbrt(np.clip(W, 0.0, None))
    A2 = A @ A
    tri = np.einsum("ij,ji->i", A2, A)
    deg = (W > 0.0).sum(axis=1).astype(float)
    denom = deg * (deg - 1.0)
    c = np.zeros_like(tri)
    ok = denom > 0.0
    c[ok] = tri[ok] / denom[ok]
    return c


def _rmt_core(
    ret: pd.DataFrame,
    win: int,
    step: int,
    shock_k: int,
    max_modes: int,
) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.Series]:
    """Rolling RMT decomposition.

    Every `step` bars we re-estimate, on the trailing `win` bars (strictly
    before the anchor), the correlation matrix, its eigen-spectrum, the
    Marchenko-Pastur edge rescaled by the top eigenvalue, the market subspace,
    the Onnela-weighted clustering / degree / eigenvector-centrality of the
    market-mode graph, and the residual (noise-subspace) volatility.  Those
    quantities are then applied to the bars of the following block, so the value
    at time t only ever uses information available at t.

    Returns (core signal frame, coupling-strength series).
    """
    idx = ret.index
    cols = ret.columns
    R = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float)
    T, N = R.shape
    core = np.full((T, N), np.nan, dtype=float)
    coup = np.full(T, np.nan, dtype=float)

    if T < win + 1 or N < 8:
        return (
            pd.DataFrame(core, index=idx, columns=cols),
            pd.Series(coup, index=idx),
        )

    finite = np.isfinite(R)
    R0 = np.where(finite, R, 0.0)

    for t0 in range(win, T, step):
        w0 = t0 - win
        t1 = min(T, t0 + step)
        Xw = R0[w0:t0]
        Fw = finite[w0:t0]

        cnt = Fw.sum(axis=0)
        sd_all = Xw.std(axis=0)
        valid = (cnt >= int(0.7 * win)) & np.isfinite(sd_all) & (sd_all > 1e-12)
        m = int(valid.sum())
        if m < 8:
            continue
        vi = np.where(valid)[0]

        Xv = Xw[:, vi]
        Fv = Fw[:, vi]
        mu = Xv.mean(axis=0)
        sdv = Xv.std(axis=0)
        sdv = np.where(sdv > 1e-12, sdv, 1.0)
        Z = np.where(Fv, (Xv - mu) / sdv, 0.0)
        Z = np.clip(Z, -8.0, 8.0)

        C = (Z.T @ Z) / float(max(win - 1, 1))
        C = np.nan_to_num(C, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
        C = 0.5 * (C + C.T)
        np.fill_diagonal(C, 1.0)

        try:
            evals, evecs = np.linalg.eigh(C)
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            continue
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(evals)):
            continue

        lam_max = float(evals[-1])
        if not np.isfinite(lam_max) or lam_max <= 0.0:
            continue

        # Rescaled Marchenko-Pastur edge (Laloux et al.): the market mode
        # absorbs lam_max/m of the total variance, so the noise bulk lives on
        # sigma^2 = 1 - lam_max/m.
        q = float(m) / float(win)
        sigma2 = max(1.0 - lam_max / float(m), 1e-3)
        lam_plus = sigma2 * (1.0 + math.sqrt(q)) ** 2

        sel = np.where(evals > lam_plus)[0]
        if sel.size == 0:
            sel = np.array([m - 1])
        if sel.size > max_modes:
            sel = sel[-max_modes:]

        V = evecs[:, sel]
        lam_sel = evals[sel]
        coupling = lam_max / float(m)

        # ---- filtered market-mode network -> topology weights ----------------
        Cm = (V * lam_sel) @ V.T
        Wm = np.abs(Cm)
        np.fill_diagonal(Wm, 0.0)
        mx = float(Wm.max())
        if not np.isfinite(mx) or mx <= 0.0:
            continue
        Wn = Wm / mx
        iu = np.triu_indices(m, 1)
        thr = max(float(np.quantile(Wn[iu], 0.85)), 0.05)
        Wt = np.where(Wn >= thr, Wn, 0.0)

        clust = _onnela_clustering(Wt)
        deg = Wt.sum(axis=1)
        evc = np.abs(evecs[:, -1])

        rc = _rank1d(clust)
        rd = _rank1d(deg)
        re_ = _rank1d(evc)
        # Redundant / hub-embedded: dense local clustering, centrality high
        # relative to raw degree.  Bridge / structural hole: many links but no
        # redundant triangles -> low score.
        redundancy = rc + 0.5 * (re_ - rd)
        wgt = 1.0 - 2.0 * _rank1d(redundancy)  # +1 bridge (ride), -1 redundant (fade)

        # ---- noise-subspace residual shocks ---------------------------------
        Ew = Z - (Z @ V) @ V.T
        sd_res = Ew.std(axis=0)
        sd_res = np.where(np.isfinite(sd_res) & (sd_res > 1e-8), sd_res, np.nan)

        seg_lo = max(0, t0 - shock_k + 1)
        Xs = R0[seg_lo:t1][:, vi]
        Fs = finite[seg_lo:t1][:, vi]
        Zs = np.where(Fs, (Xs - mu) / sdv, 0.0)
        Zs = np.clip(Zs, -8.0, 8.0)
        Es = Zs - (Zs @ V) @ V.T

        cs = np.cumsum(Es, axis=0)
        denom = sd_res * math.sqrt(float(shock_k))

        for t in range(t0, t1):
            j = t - seg_lo
            if j < shock_k - 1:
                continue
            roll = cs[j] - (cs[j - shock_k] if j >= shock_k else 0.0)
            shock = roll / denom
            shock = np.clip(np.nan_to_num(shock, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0), -5.0, 5.0)
            core[t, vi] = wgt * shock
            coup[t] = coupling

    return (
        pd.DataFrame(core, index=idx, columns=cols),
        pd.Series(coup, index=idx),
    )


@register_factor
class RmtNoiseShockClusteringRedundancySwitch(BaseFactor):
    """Noise-subspace residual shock, sign-switched by market-mode network redundancy."""

    factor_id = "rmt_noise_shock_clustering_redundancy_switch"
    name = "RMT Noise-Subspace Shock with Network-Redundancy Sign Switch"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "On a rolling window of 10-second log returns, eigendecompose the "
        "cross-sectional correlation matrix, define the market subspace as the "
        "eigenvalues exceeding the top-eigenvalue-rescaled Marchenko-Pastur edge, "
        "project it out to obtain each name's standardized noise-subspace shock, "
        "then multiply that shock by a centered cross-sectional weight built from "
        "the Onnela-weighted local clustering coefficient (plus degree and "
        "eigenvector centrality) of the thresholded market-mode graph, so that "
        "redundant hub-embedded names get a reversal sign and low-clustering "
        "bridge names a continuation sign, with the whole signal scaled by the "
        "top eigenvalue's explained-variance share."
    )
    window_length = 260
    inputs = ["close"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # estimation geometry
    _WIN = 180        # trailing bars used for the correlation matrix (~30 min)
    _STEP = 30        # re-estimate the spectrum / network every 30 bars (~5 min)
    _SHOCK_K = 3      # residual shock accumulated over the last 3 bars (~30 s)
    _MAX_MODES = 10   # cap on the number of retained market modes

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        px = close.replace(0.0, np.nan).astype(float)
        px = px.where(px > 0.0)

        logp = np.log(px)
        ret = logp.diff()
        ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        # kill absurd prints so a single bad tick cannot define the eigen-basis
        ret = ret.clip(-0.2, 0.2)

        core, coup = _rmt_core(
            ret,
            int(self._WIN),
            int(self._STEP),
            int(self._SHOCK_K),
            int(self._MAX_MODES),
        )

        # cross-sectional standardisation of the sign-switched residual shock
        row_mu = core.mean(axis=1)
        row_sd = core.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        z = core.sub(row_mu, axis=0).div(row_sd, axis=0)
        z = z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-4.0, 4.0)

        # coupling-strength amplitude: top eigenvalue variance share relative to
        # its own slow trailing level (causal exponential mean)
        c = coup.ffill()
        base = c.ewm(halflife=2000, min_periods=1).mean()
        amp = (c / base.replace(0.0, np.nan)).replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        amp = amp.clip(0.25, 4.0).fillna(1.0)

        out = z.mul(amp, axis=0)
        out = out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        out = out.where(close.notna(), 0.0)
        return out.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:

        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, ts_mean, ts_zscore
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _clip_z(df: pd.DataFrame, lo: float = -3.0, hi: float = 3.0) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Bounded, NaN-safe standardised feature in roughly [-1, 1]."""
    return (df.clip(lo, hi) / hi).fillna(0.0)


def _naive_forecaster(
    open_: pd.DataFrame,
    high: pd.DataFrame,
    low: pd.DataFrame,
    close: pd.DataFrame,
    volume: pd.DataFrame,
):
    """Build the 'announced' log-odds z_t and the control block c_t.

    All inputs are bar-t quantities, so the vector returned at index t is known
    at the close of bar t and is used to forecast the direction of bar t+1.
    """
    rng = (high - low)
    rng_safe = rng.replace(0.0, np.nan)

    # 1) close-location value inside the bar range
    clv = ((2.0 * close - high - low) / rng_safe).clip(-1.0, 1.0).fillna(0.0)

    # 2) signed volume pressure, standardised against its own trailing norm
    signed_vol = np.sign(close - open_) * volume.clip(lower=0.0)
    press = _clip_z(ts_zscore(signed_vol, 60))

    # 3) run persistence of the last few tick directions
    step = np.sign(close.diff()).fillna(0.0)
    run = ts_mean(step, 5).fillna(0.0).clip(-1.0, 1.0)

    # announced log-odds: deliberately modest, p in ~[0.18, 0.82]
    z = (0.60 * clv + 0.50 * press + 0.60 * run).clip(-1.5, 1.5)

    # controls c_t: intercept, relative-range (volatility) state, volume state
    ones = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
    vol_state = _clip_z(ts_zscore((rng / close.replace(0.0, np.nan)), 60))
    trade_state = _clip_z(ts_zscore(np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0)), 60))

    controls = [ones, vol_state, trade_state]
    return z, controls


def _online_trust_betting(
    U: np.ndarray,
    z: np.ndarray,
    up: np.ndarray,
    moved: np.ndarray,
    valid: np.ndarray,
    lam_w: float,
    lam_e: float,
    ridge_w: float,
    ridge_e: float,
    min_obs: int,
    kappa: float,
) -> np.ndarray:
    """Per-ticker online logistic recalibration + game-theoretic capital process.

    U      : (T, N, d) design vectors, U[t] known at close of bar t.
    z      : (T, N) announced log-odds (U[..., 0] == z).
    up     : (T, N) outcome 1{close_t > close_{t-1}}  (realised *during* bar t).
    moved  : (T, N) bar-t price actually changed (ties are treated as no game).
    valid  : (T, N) design vector is finite.

    At loop step t the state is first updated with the pair
    (U[t-1], up[t]) -- whose outcome only becomes known at the close of bar t --
    and only then is the bet for bar t+1 formed from U[t].  Hence the value
    emitted at index t uses information available at t and nothing later.
    """
    T, N, d = U.shape
    eye = np.eye(d)

    # --- recalibration model state: P_w = V_w^{-1}, prior beta = 1 (full trust)
    Pw = np.repeat((eye / ridge_w)[None, :, :], N, axis=0)
    w = np.zeros((N, d))
    w[:, 0] = 1.0

    # --- capital-process state
    Pe = np.repeat((eye / ridge_e)[None, :, :], N, axis=0)
    S = np.zeros((N, d))
    logdet = np.zeros(N)
    cnt = np.zeros(N)

    out = np.full((T, N), np.nan)

    p_face_prev = np.full(N, 0.5)
    u_prev = np.zeros((N, d))
    valid_prev = np.zeros(N, dtype=bool)

    for t in range(T):
        if t > 0:
            y = up[t]
            obs = valid_prev & np.isfinite(y) & moved[t]
            if obs.any():
                u = np.where(obs[:, None], u_prev, 0.0)
                yv = np.where(obs, np.nan_to_num(y, nan=0.0), 0.0)

                # ---- exponentially-weighted recursive IRLS (online Newton) ----
                eta = np.clip((u * w).sum(axis=1), -8.0, 8.0)
                phat = special.expit(eta)
                s = np.where(obs, np.clip(phat * (1.0 - phat), 1e-4, 0.25), 0.0)
                lam = np.where(obs, lam_w, 1.0)

                Pu = np.einsum("nij,nj->ni", Pw, u)
                uPu = np.clip((u * Pu).sum(axis=1), 0.0, None)
                den = lam + s * uPu
                Pw = (
                    Pw
                    - (s / den)[:, None, None] * Pu[:, :, None] * Pu[:, None, :]
                ) / lam[:, None, None]

                Pu_new = np.einsum("nij,nj->ni", Pw, u)
                w = w + Pu_new * ((yv - phat) * obs)[:, None]
                w = np.clip(w, -8.0, 8.0)

                # ---- game-theoretic capital process on the announced odds ----
                pf = np.where(obs, np.clip(p_face_prev, 1e-3, 1.0 - 1e-3), 0.5)
                se = np.where(obs, np.clip(pf * (1.0 - pf), 1e-4, 0.25), 0.0)
                lame = np.where(obs, lam_e, 1.0)

                Peu = np.einsum("nij,nj->ni", Pe, u)
                uPeu = np.clip((u * Peu).sum(axis=1), 0.0, None)
                dene = lame + se * uPeu
                logdet = (
                    logdet
                    + d * np.log(lame)
                    + np.log1p(np.clip(se * uPeu / lame, 0.0, None))
                )
                Pe = (
                    Pe
                    - (se / dene)[:, None, None] * Peu[:, :, None] * Peu[:, None, :]
                ) / lame[:, None, None]
                S = lame[:, None] * S + u * ((yv - pf) * obs)[:, None]

                cnt = cnt + obs.astype(float)

        # ---------- form the bet for the next bar from information at t -------
        v = valid[t]
        u_t = np.where(v[:, None], np.nan_to_num(U[t], nan=0.0), 0.0)
        eta_t = np.clip((u_t * w).sum(axis=1), -8.0, 8.0)
        phat_t = special.expit(eta_t)
        p_t = special.expit(np.clip(np.nan_to_num(z[t], nan=0.0), -8.0, 8.0))
        p_t = np.clip(p_t, 1e-3, 1.0 - 1e-3)

        nu = np.clip((phat_t - p_t) / (p_t * (1.0 - p_t)), -20.0, 20.0)

        PeS = np.einsum("nij,nj->ni", Pe, S)
        evid = np.clip((S * PeS).sum(axis=1), 0.0, None)
        gate = np.tanh(evid / (np.maximum(logdet, 1.0) * kappa))

        sig = nu * gate
        ok = v & (cnt >= min_obs) & np.isfinite(sig)
        out[t] = np.where(ok, sig, np.nan)

        u_prev = u_t
        valid_prev = v
        p_face_prev = p_t

    return out

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):

basket is stale (the paper's central friction). It dies if the gap is driven by
genuine idiosyncratic news, in which case high-gap names should continue to diverge
rather than converge, and if the signal survives only in the sparse support names
themselves (the opposite of the transmission story).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import (
    correlation,
    rank,
    rolling_beta,
    stddev,
    ts_sum,
)
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- parameters
_W_EST = 360          # estimation window for the replication problem (bars)
_K_REFIT = 60         # re-estimate the sparse basket every K bars
_N_SEL = 12           # max holdings per greedy replication pass
_NAME_CAP = 0.20      # per-name coefficient cap (non-negative weights)
_SEC_FRAC = 0.40      # per-sector cap, as a fraction of _N_SEL holdings
_N_BOOT = 8           # bootstrap sub-windows for stability selection
_BLOCK = 20           # block length of the block bootstrap (bars)
_MIN_FREQ = 0.375     # inclusion-frequency threshold to enter the basket
_RB = 180             # trailing window for loading / R-squared
_L_GAP = 3            # short-horizon transmission window (bars)
_SEED = 20230917      # fixed seed -> deterministic output


def _safe_returns(close: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Causal bar returns, de-spiked."""
    ret = close.pct_change()
    ret = ret.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
    return ret.clip(-0.25, 0.25)


def _cap_weighted_market(ret: pd.DataFrame, mcap: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.Series:
    """Cap-weighted market return using *lagged* (already point-in-time) caps."""
    w = mcap.shift(1).abs()
    w = w.where(np.isfinite(w))
    w = w.where(ret.notna())
    num = (w * ret.fillna(0.0)).sum(axis=1)
    den = w.sum(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    mkt = num / den
    return mkt.fillna(ret.mean(axis=1)).fillna(0.0)


def _mp_select(
    rw: np.ndarray,
    mw: np.ndarray,
    sec: np.ndarray,
    elig: np.ndarray,
    n_sel: int,
    name_cap: float,
    max_per_sec: int,
):
    """Greedy non-negative, name-capped, sector-capped matching pursuit.

    Replicates the benchmark path ``mw`` with a sparse non-negative combination of
    the columns of ``rw``.  Only positive projections are ever accepted, so every
    accumulated coefficient is >= 0 (the paper's long-only tracking constraint);
    a name is retired once its coefficient hits ``name_cap`` and a whole sector is
    retired once it holds ``max_per_sec`` distinct names.  Purely trailing data.
    """
    n = rw.shape[1]
    resid = np.asarray(mw, dtype=float).copy()
    coef = np.zeros(n, dtype=float)
    selected = np.zeros(n, dtype=bool)
    active = np.asarray(elig, dtype=bool).copy()

    denom = (rw * rw).sum(axis=0)
    active = active & (denom > 0.0)
    norm = np.sqrt(np.where(denom > 0.0, denom, np.nan))

    sec_counts: dict[int, int] = {}

    for _ in range(int(n_sel) * 2):
        if not active.any():
            break
        num = rw.T.dot(resid)
        with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
            score = num / norm
        score = np.where(np.isfinite(score) & active, score, -np.inf)
        j = int(np.argmax(score))
        if not np.isfinite(score[j]) or score[j] <= 0.0:
            break
        c = num[j] / denom[j]
        if c <= 0.0:
            active[j] = False
            continue
        room = name_cap - coef[j]
        if room <= 1e-12:
            active[j] = False
            continue
        c = min(c, room)
        coef[j] += c
        resid = resid - c * rw[:, j]
        if not selected[j]:
            selected[j] = True
            s = int(sec[j])
            sec_counts[s] = sec_counts.get(s, 0) + 1
            if sec_counts[s] >= max_per_sec:
                active = active & ~((sec == s) & ~selected)
        if coef[j] >= name_cap - 1e-12:
            active[j] = False
        if int(selected.sum()) >= int(n_sel):
            break

    return selected, coef


def _stability_frequency(
    rw: np.ndarray,
    mw: np.ndarray,
    sec: np.ndarray,
    elig: np.ndarray,
    n_sel: int,
    name_cap: float,
    max_per_sec: int,
    n_boot: int,
    block: int,
    rng: np.random.Generator,
):
    """Inclusion frequency across block-bootstrapped sub-windows.

    The paper's 'count of holdings' weighting: a name's weight is how *often* the
    sparse replication picks it, not how large its coefficient is.
    """
    t, n = rw.shape
    counts = np.zeros(n, dtype=float)
    coefs = np.zeros(n, dtype=float)
    sub_len = max(block, t // 2)
    nblocks = max(1, int(sub_len // block))
    hi = max(1, t - block)

    for _ in range(int(n_boot)):
        starts = rng.integers(0, hi, size=nblocks)
        idxs = np.concatenate([np.arange(s, s + block) for s in starts])
        idxs = np.clip(idxs, 0, t - 1)
        sel, coef = _mp_select(
            rw[idxs, :], mw[idxs], sec, elig, n_sel, name_cap, max_per_sec
        )
        counts += sel.astype(float)
        coefs += coef

    return counts / float(n_boot), coefs / float(n_boot)


@register_factor
class StabilitySelectedSparseBasketLagGap(BaseFactor):
    """Gap between a stability-selected sparse tracking basket's implied return and
    each stock's realized return, gated to the slow periphery of the basket."""

    factor_id = "stability_selected_sparse_basket_lag_gap"
    name = "Stability-Selected Sparse Tracking Basket Transmission Gap"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Every K bars a sparse, non-negative, name- and sector-capped basket "
        "replicating the cap-weighted market return is built by stability "
        "selection (inclusion frequency across block-bootstrapped sub-windows as "
        "the weight). Each stock gets a trailing loading and R-squared on the "
        "leave-one-out basket; the signal is the cross-sectional rank of the "
        "short-horizon gap (loading x cumulative basket return minus own "
        "cumulative return), gated up for names outside the sparse support and "
        "for names the basket explains well."
    )
    window_length = 600
    inputs = ["close", "marketCap", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        idx = close.index
        cols = close.columns
        empty = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)

        n_bars = len(idx)
        n_names = len(cols)
        if n_bars < _W_EST + _L_GAP + 5 or n_names < 6:
            return empty

        ret = _safe_returns(close)

        mcap = data.get("marketCap")
        if mcap is None:
            mcap = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)
        else:
            mcap = mcap.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).ffill()
            if not np.isfinite(mcap.to_numpy(dtype=float, na_value=np.nan)).any():
                mcap = pd.DataFrame(1.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        mkt = _cap_weighted_market(ret, mcap)

        sector = data.get("sector")
        if sector is not None:
            sector = sector.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).ffill()

        ret_np = ret.to_numpy(dtype=float)
        mkt_np = mkt.to_numpy(dtype=float)

        freq_arr = np.full((n_bars, n_names), np.nan, dtype=float)
        w_arr = np.full((n_bars, n_names), np.nan, dtype=float)

        rng = np.random.default_rng(_SEED)

        refit_rows = list(range(_W_EST - 1, n_bars, _K_REFIT))
        for row in refit_rows:
            lo = row - _W_EST + 1
            rw_raw = ret_np[lo : row + 1, :]
            mw_raw = mkt_np[lo : row + 1]

            good_frac = np.isfinite(rw_raw).mean(axis=0)
            rw = np.nan_to_num(rw_raw, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
            mw = np.nan_to_num(mw_raw, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
            sd = rw.std(axis=0)
            elig = (good_frac >= 0.8) & (sd > 0.0)
            if int(elig.sum()) < 5:
                continue

            if sector is not None:
                labels = sector.iloc[row].astype(object).fillna("__NA__")
                codes = pd.factorize(labels.to_numpy())[0].astype(int)
            else:
                codes = np.zeros(n_names, dtype=int)

            n_sec = int(len(np.unique(codes[elig])))
            if n_sec <= 1:
                max_per_sec = int(_N_SEL)
            else:
                max_per_sec = max(2, int(math.ceil(_N_SEL * _SEC_FRAC)))

            freq, _coef = _stability_frequency(
                rw,
                mw,
                codes,
                elig,
                _N_SEL,
                _NAME_CAP,
                max_per_sec,
                _N_BOOT,
                _BLOCK,
                rng,
            )

            wts = np.where(freq >= _MIN_FREQ, freq, 0.0)
            tot = wts.sum()
            if tot <= 0.0:
                continue
            wts = wts / tot

            freq_arr[row, :] = freq
            w_arr[row, :] = wts

        freq_df = pd.DataFrame(freq_arr, index=idx, columns=cols).ffill().shift(1)
        w_df = pd.DataFrame(w_arr, index=idx, columns=cols).ffill().shift(1)

        if not np.isfinite(w_df.to_numpy(dtype=float)).any():
            return empty

        # ---- basket return, leave-one-out so a support name is not its own hub
        ret0 = ret.fillna(0.0)
        wm = w_df.where(ret.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
        contrib = wm * ret0
        num_tot = contrib.sum(axis=1)
        den_tot = wm.sum(axis=1)

        num_excl = (-contrib).add(num_tot, axis=0)
        den_excl = (-wm).add(den_tot, axis=0)
        den_excl = den_excl.where(den_excl > 0.30)
        basket = num_excl / den_excl
        basket = basket.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).clip(-0.25, 0.25)

        # ---- causal loading and explanatory power on the sparse basket
        beta = rolling_beta(ret, basket, _RB).clip(-1.0, 4.0)
        r2 = correlation(ret, basket, _RB) ** 2.0

        # ---- short-horizon transmission gap: owed move minus realised move
        gap = beta * ts_sum(basket, _L_GAP) - ts_sum(ret, _L_GAP)
        vol = stddev(ret, _RB).replace(0.0, np.nan) * math.sqrt(float(_L_GAP))
        zgap = (gap / vol).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        # ---- gate: periphery names (low inclusion frequency), well-explained
        periphery = (1.0 - freq_df.clip(0.0, 1.0)).fillna(1.0)
        gate_p = 0.20 + 0.80 * periphery
        gate_r2 = 0.20 + 0.80 * rank(r2)

        gated = zgap * gate_p * gate_r2
        gated = gated.where(np.isfinite(gated))

        out = rank(gated) - 0.5
        return out.where(gated.notna()).reindex(index=idx, columns=cols)
"}

    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""

        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy import special

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor

_CHARS = [
    "earningsYield",
    "pbRatio",
    "marketCap",
    "roe",
    "debtToEquity",
    "assetGrowth",
    "grossMargin",
    "freeCashFlowYield",
]

_K = 3            # pursuit iterations (assumed sparsity of active baskets)
_MAX_SECTORS = 12  # cap on sector dummy atoms


def _row_demean_unitnorm(df: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Mask to the tradable universe, cross-sectionally demean, then unit-norm each row.

    Purely row-wise (uses only information from the same bar) so it is causal.
    """
    x = df.astype(float).where(mask)
    x = x.sub(x.mean(axis=1), axis=0)
    x = x.where(mask, 0.0).fillna(0.0)
    nrm = np.sqrt((x * x).sum(axis=1)).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    out = x.div(nrm, axis=0)
    return out.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)


def _build_atoms(
    data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame], mask: pd.DataFrame
) -> list[pd.DataFrame]:
    """Unit-norm dictionary: sector dummies + rank-standardised characteristic loadings."""
    atoms: list[pd.DataFrame] = []

    sec = data.get("sector")
    if sec is not None:
        try:
            flat = pd.Series(np.asarray(sec.values).ravel())
            flat = flat[flat.notna()].astype(str)
            labels = [str(l) for l in flat.value_counts().index[:_MAX_SECTORS]]
        except Exception:
            labels = []
        if len(labels) > 1:
            sec_str = sec.astype(str)
            for lab in labels:
                dm = (sec_str == lab).astype(float)
                a = _row_demean_unitnorm(dm, mask)
                if float(a.abs().values.sum()) > 0.0:
                    atoms.append(a)

    for fld in _CHARS:
        x = data.get(fld)
        if x is None:
            continue
        try:
            xf = x.astype(float)
        except Exception:
            continue
        loading = rank(xf)
        a = _row_demean_unitnorm(loading, mask)
        if float(a.abs().values.sum()) > 0.0:
            atoms.append(a)

    return atoms


def _coefs(atoms: list[pd.DataFrame], r: pd.DataFrame) -> np.ndarray:
    """Row-wise inner products <atom_j, r> -> (T, M) array of projection coefficients."""
    rv = r.values
    return np.column_stack([(a.values * rv).sum(axis=1) for a in atoms])


def _weighted_atom(
    atoms: list[pd.DataFrame], w: np.ndarray, index, columns
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Sum_j w[:, j] * atom_j  (w is a per-bar one-hot / weight matrix)."""
    out = None
    for j, a in enumerate(atoms):
        wj = w[:, j]
        if not np.any(wj):
            continue
        contrib = a.mul(pd.Series(wj, index=index), axis=0)
        out = contrib if out is None else out + contrib
    if out is None:
        return pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=index, columns=columns)
    return out


def _row_zscore(df: pd.DataFrame, mask: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    x = df.where(mask)
    sd = x.std(axis=1).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    z = x.sub(x.mean(axis=1), axis=0).div(sd, axis=0)
    return z.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)


@register_factor
class MapSupportPursuitFactorImpulseSplit(BaseFactor):
    """MAP-gOMP split of each bar's cross-section into a persistent detected basket
    impulse (long) and a mean-reverting unexplained residual (short)."""

    factor_id = "map_support_pursuit_factor_impulse_split"
    name = (
        "MAP-Support Greedy Pursuit: Sparse Characteristic-Basket Impulse vs. "
        "Idiosyncratic Residual"
    )
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Each bar, a K=3 greedy pursuit of the cross-sectionally standardised bar "
        "return onto a unit-norm dictionary of sector dummies and rank-standardised "
        "fundamental characteristic loadings, selecting atoms by the log-MAP ratio "
        "(residual-variance-scaled Gaussian likelihood ratio with effective noise "
        "variance shrinking as atoms are resolved, plus a log-odds prior from each "
        "atom's trailing activation frequency) instead of largest |correlation|. "
        "Signal = confidence-weighted, Wiener-shrunk, short-EWMA-persisted "
        "projection of the detected atom coefficients onto each stock's loadings "
        "minus the standardised unexplained residual."
    )
    window_length = 240
    inputs = [
        "close",
        "sector",
        "earningsYield",
        "pbRatio",
        "marketCap",
        "roe",
        "debtToEquity",
        "assetGrowth",
        "grossMargin",
        "freeCashFlowYield",
    ]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        idx, cols = close.index, close.columns
        zeros = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=idx, columns=cols)

        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        mask = ret.notna()
        n_ok = mask.sum(axis=1)
        row_ok = n_ok >= 5
        mask = mask.mul(row_ok.astype(int), axis=0).astype(bool)
        if not bool(mask.values.any()):
            return zeros

        n_valid = mask.sum(axis=1).astype(float).clip(lower=1.0)

        # ---- measurement vector: cross-sectionally standardised, winsorised returns
        z = _row_zscore(ret, mask)
        z = z.where(mask, 0.0).fillna(0.0).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        atoms = _build_atoms(data, mask)
        M = len(atoms)
        T = len(idx)
        if M < 2:
            return zeros

        atom_ok = np.column_stack(
            [(a.abs().sum(axis=1) > 0.0).values for a in atoms]
        )
        rows = np.arange(T)
        neg_inf = -np.inf

        # =================================================================
        # Stage A - plain max-|correlation| OMP control pass.  Used ONLY to
        # build (lagged) nuisance estimates: atom activation priors, signal
        # coefficient variance and residual (noise) variance.
        # =================================================================
        rA = z.copy()
        chosenA = np.zeros((T, M), dtype=bool)
        actA = np.zeros((T, M))
        c2_top = np.zeros(T)

        for k in range(_K):
            C = _coefs(atoms, rA)
            S = np.abs(C)
            S = np.where(np.isfinite(S), S, neg_inf)
            S = np.where(atom_ok, S, neg_inf)
            S = np.where(chosenA, neg_inf, S)
            sel = np.argmax(S, axis=1)
            best = S[rows, sel]
            hit = np.isfinite(best) & (best > 0.0)
            I = np.zeros((T, M))
            I[rows, sel] = np.where(hit, 1.0, 0.0)
            if k == 0:
                c2_top = (C[rows, sel] ** 2) * hit.astype(float)
            chosenA = chosenA | (I > 0.0)
            actA = actA + I
            csel = (C * I).sum(axis=1)
            dsel = _weighted_atom(atoms, I, idx, cols)
            rA = rA - dsel.mul(pd.Series(csel, index=idx), axis=0)

        # noise variance per cross-sectional component (trailing, lagged)
        res_energy = (rA * rA).sum(axis=1) / n_valid
        sigma_n2 = (
            res_energy.ewm(halflife=30, min_periods=5).mean().shift(1)
        ).clip(lower=1e-10)

        # prior variance of an active atom's coefficient (trailing, lagged)
        sigma_a2 = (
            pd.Series(c2_top, index=idx)
            .ewm(halflife=60, min_periods=5)
            .mean()
            .shift(1)
        ).clip(lower=1e-10)

        # activation prior p_j from trailing activation frequency (lagged)
        act_df = pd.DataFrame(np.clip(actA, 0.0, 1.0), index=idx)
        p = (
            act_df.ewm(halflife=120, min_periods=10)
            .mean()
            .shift(1)
            .fillna(float(_K) / float(M))
            .clip(0.02, 0.98)
        )
        logit_p = np.log(p.values / (1.0 - p.values))

        sa2 = sigma_a2.values
        sn2 = sigma_n2.values
        nv = n_valid.values

        # =================================================================
        # Stage B - MAP support detection (MAP-gOMP): select by log posterior
        # odds, with effective noise variance shrinking as atoms are resolved.
        # =================================================================
        rB = z.copy()
        impulse = zeros.copy()
        chosenB = np.zeros((T, M), dtype=bool)

        for k in range(_K):
            C = _coefs(atoms, rB)
            remaining = max(_K - 1 - k, 0)
            se2 = sn2 + remaining * sa2 / nv
            se2 = np.where(np.isfinite(se2), se2, np.nan)
            se2 = np.maximum(se2, 1e-10)
            snr = sa2 / se2
            gain = sa2 / (sa2 + se2)          # Wiener / posterior-mean shrinkage
            lr = (
                0.5 * (C ** 2) * (sa2 / (se2 * (sa2 + se2)))[:, None]
                - 0.5 * np.log1p(snr)[:, None]
                + logit_p
            )
            lr = np.where(np.isfinite(lr), lr, neg_inf)
            lr = np.where(atom_ok, lr, neg_inf)
            lr = np.where(chosenB, neg_inf, lr)
            sel = np.argmax(lr, axis=1)
            score = lr[rows, sel]
            detected = np.isfinite(score) & (score > 0.0)

            I = np.zeros((T, M))
            I[rows, sel] = np.where(detected, 1.0, 0.0)
            chosenB = chosenB | (I > 0.0)

            csel = (C * I).sum(axis=1)
            conf = special.expit(np.clip(score, -50.0, 50.0)) * detected.astype(float)
            g = np.where(np.isfinite(gain), gain, 0.0)
            w_imp = np.nan_to_num(conf * g * csel, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)
            w_res = np.nan_to_num(csel, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0)

            dsel = _weighted_atom(atoms, I, idx, cols)
            impulse = impulse + dsel.mul(pd.Series(w_imp, index=idx), axis=0)
            rB = rB - dsel.mul(pd.Series(w_res, index=idx), axis=0)

        # ---- persistence of the detected basket impulse (parents unfold slowly)
        imp_p = impulse.fillna(0.0).ewm(halflife=2.0, min_periods=1).mean()
        imp_z = _row_zscore(imp_p, mask).fillna(0.0).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        # ---- unexplained residual: quote noise / liquidity overshoot -> reverts
        res_z = _row_zscore(rB, mask).fillna(0.0).clip(-6.0, 6.0)

        combined = (imp_z - res_z).where(mask)
        return rank(combined)

    """Variance-ratio regime factor: fade names whose returns mean-revert."""

    from __future__ import annotations

    import numpy as np
    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, stddev, ts_mean
from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


def _orthonormal_patch_basis(n_patch: int) -> dict[str, np.ndarray]:
    """Build an orthonormal shape basis over ``n_patch`` chronological patches.

    Columns are ordered constant -> linear (trend) -> quadratic (curvature) ->
    Haar (level shift) -> alternating (Nyquist / quote bounce) and then
    Gram-Schmidt'd via a QR factorisation, so each later axis carries only the
    part of the shape *not* already explained by the earlier, smoother axes.
    This is a deterministic, data-independent construction (no fitting).
    """
    idx = np.arange(n_patch, dtype=float)
    centred = idx - idx.mean()

    const = np.ones(n_patch)
    linear = centred
    quad = centred ** 2 - np.mean(centred ** 2)

    haar = np.where(idx >= n_patch / 2.0, 1.0, -1.0)          # newest half = +1
    alt = np.array([(-1.0) ** (n_patch - 1 - i) for i in range(n_patch)])  # newest = +1

    design = np.column_stack([const, linear, quad, haar, alt])
    q_mat, r_mat = np.linalg.qr(design)

    # Fix sign convention so each orthonormal axis points the same way as the
    # raw pattern it was seeded from (positive R diagonal).
    diag = np.diag(r_mat)
    signs = np.where(diag < 0.0, -1.0, 1.0)
    q_mat = q_mat * signs[np.newaxis, :]

    return {
        "slope": q_mat[:, 1],
        "curvature": q_mat[:, 2],
        "step": q_mat[:, 3],
        "alternating": q_mat[:, 4],
    }


_BASIS = _orthonormal_patch_basis(6)


def _patch_means(df: pd.DataFrame, patch: int, n_patch: int) -> list[pd.DataFrame]:
    """Non-overlapping trailing patch means, oldest first, all causal.

    Patch i (i = 0 is the oldest) is the mean of the ``patch`` bars ending
    ``patch * (n_patch - 1 - i)`` bars ago, so the newest patch ends at t.
    """
    base = ts_mean(df, patch)
    return [base.shift(patch * (n_patch - 1 - i)) for i in range(n_patch)]


def _z_shape(patches: list[pd.DataFrame]) -> list[pd.DataFrame]:
    """Within-window z-normalisation across patches -> scale-free shape vector."""
    n = float(len(patches))
    total = patches[0]
    for p in patches[1:]:
        total = total + p
    mean = total / n

    var = None
    for p in patches:
        sq = (p - mean) ** 2
        var = sq if var is None else var + sq
    var = var / n
    sd = np.sqrt(var).replace(0.0, np.nan)
    return [(p - mean) / sd for p in patches]


def _project(z_patches: list[pd.DataFrame], vec: np.ndarray) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Inner product of the shape vector with one orthonormal basis axis."""
    out = None
    for w, z in zip(vec, z_patches):
        term = z * float(w)
        out = term if out is None else out + term
    return out

class PatchShapeBasisScaleContextGate(BaseFactor):
    """Patch-normalized shape basis (step vs Nyquist) gated by volume confirmation and amplitude context."""

    factor_id = "patch_shape_basis_scale_context_gate"
    name = "Patch-Shape Basis Decomposition with Scale & Volume Context Gate"
    category = "microstructure"
    description = (
        "For each ticker, the last 36 bars of close are split into 6 "
        "non-overlapping patches; patch means are z-normalized within the "
        "window to give a scale-free 6-dim shape vector, which is projected "
        "onto an orthonormal discrete basis (linear/slope, quadratic/curvature, "
        "Haar step, alternating Nyquist). The same patching is applied to "
        "volume to build a confirmation weight; the final cross-sectionally "
        "ranked score is +step*confirmation (persistence) minus unconfirmed "
        "step, minus the alternating component, all scaled by the window "
        "amplitude relative to the name's own longer-run amplitude (scale "
        "context re-injection)."
    )
    window_length = 420
    inputs = ["close", "volume"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    # patching geometry
    _patch = 6
    _n_patch = 6
    _long_window = 360

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"]
        volume = data["volume"]

        patch = self._patch
        n_patch = self._n_patch

        # ---- channel 1: price path -> scale-free patch shape ----------------
        px_patches = _patch_means(close, patch, n_patch)
        px_z = _z_shape(px_patches)

        step_c = _project(px_z, _BASIS["step"])          # level-shift axis
        alt_c = _project(px_z, _BASIS["alternating"])    # quote-bounce axis

        # ---- channel 2 (tagged parallel stream): volume patches -------------
        vol = np.log1p(volume.clip(lower=0.0).fillna(0.0))
        vol_patches = _patch_means(vol, patch, n_patch)
        vol_z = _z_shape(vol_patches)
        vol_step = _project(vol_z, _BASIS["step"]).clip(-3.0, 3.0)

        # confirmation in [-1, 1]: +1 = volume stepped up together with price,
        # -1 = volume went quiet while price stepped (liquidity artefact).
        conf = np.tanh(vol_step).fillna(0.0)

        # ---- scale context re-injection -------------------------------------
        ret = close.pct_change().replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)
        amp_short = stddev(ret, patch * n_patch)
        amp_long = stddev(ret, self._long_window).replace(0.0, np.nan)
        gate = (amp_short / amp_long).clip(0.0, 3.0).fillna(1.0)

        # ---- combine: confirmed step persists, unconfirmed step and the
        #      alternating (Nyquist) component revert ---------------------------
        raw = gate * (step_c * conf - alt_c)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        out = rank(raw) - 0.5
        return out.reindex(index=close.index, columns=close.columns).fillna(0.0)

def _ols1_resid_var(y: np.ndarray, x: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Trailing-window OLS y ~ a + b*x, column-wise; returns residual variance."""
    n = max(int(y.shape[0]), 1)
    yc = y - y.mean(0)
    xc = x - x.mean(0)
    sxx = (xc * xc).sum(0) / n
    sxy = (xc * yc).sum(0) / n
    good = sxx > 0.0
    b = np.where(good, sxy / np.where(good, sxx, 1.0), 0.0)
    res = yc - b * xc
    return (res * res).sum(0) / n


def _ols2_resid_var(y: np.ndarray, x1: np.ndarray, x2: np.ndarray):
    """Two-regressor OLS (plus intercept via centring), closed form per column.

    Returns (residual variance, coefficient on x2).  Purely trailing: the caller
    only ever passes windows ending at the current bar.
    """
    n = max(int(y.shape[0]), 1)
    yc = y - y.mean(0)
    a1 = x1 - x1.mean(0)
    a2 = x2 - x2.mean(0)
    s11 = (a1 * a1).sum(0) / n
    s22 = (a2 * a2).sum(0) / n
    s12 = (a1 * a2).sum(0) / n
    sy1 = (a1 * yc).sum(0) / n
    sy2 = (a2 * yc).sum(0) / n
    det = s11 * s22 - s12 * s12
    good = det > 1e-8 * np.maximum(s11 * s22, 1e-300)
    safe_det = np.where(good, det, 1.0)
    safe_s22 = np.where(s22 > 0.0, s22, 1.0)
    b1 = np.where(good, (s22 * sy1 - s12 * sy2) / safe_det, 0.0)
    b2_fallback = np.where(s22 > 0.0, sy2 / safe_s22, 0.0)
    b2 = np.where(good, (s11 * sy2 - s12 * sy1) / safe_det, b2_fallback)
    res = yc - b1 * a1 - b2 * a2
    var = (res * res).sum(0) / n
    return var, b2


def _banded_dtw_panel(Xn: np.ndarray, Yn: np.ndarray, Yraw: np.ndarray, band: int):
    """Sakoe-Chiba band-limited DTW, vectorised across the ticker cross-section.

    Xn, Yn : (W, N) volatility-normalised cumulative log-price paths (follower,
             leader).  Yraw : (W, N) leader path in raw log-return units.
    Alignment is anchored at the window start (0, 0) and left *open at the
    leader end*, so the endpoint of the warping path gives the current
    (variable) lag Δ_T = i_end - j_end.

    Returns (s_score, lag, yhat, norm_cost):
      s_score   : mean sign of the warp offsets i_k - j_k  (emulation direction)
      lag       : endpoint lag Δ_T in bars (may be negative)
      yhat      : (W, N) warp-reconstructed leader path on the follower clock
      norm_cost : length-normalised alignment distance (similarity)
    Everything is a trailing-window computation: no future information is used.
    """
    W, N = Xn.shape
    K = 2 * band + 1
    inf = np.inf

    Ypad = np.full((W + 2 * band, N), np.nan)
    Ypad[band:band + W, :] = Yn
    Cost = np.empty((W, K, N))
    for k in range(K):
        Cost[:, k, :] = (Xn - Ypad[k:k + W, :]) ** 2
    Cost[~np.isfinite(Cost)] = inf

    D = np.full((W, K, N), inf)
    D[0, band, :] = Cost[0, band, :]
    inf_row = np.full(N, inf)

    for i in range(1, W):
        Dprev = D[i - 1]
        Dcur = D[i]
        Ci = Cost[i]
        jlo = i - band
        if jlo < 0:
            jlo = 0
        jhi = i + band
        if jhi > W - 1:
            jhi = W - 1
        for j in range(jlo, jhi + 1):
            k = j - i + band
            if (k + 1) < K:
                m = Dprev[k + 1]          # step from (i-1, j)
            else:
                m = inf_row
            if j >= 1:
                m = np.minimum(m, Dprev[k])       # diagonal (i-1, j-1)
                if k >= 1:
                    m = np.minimum(m, Dcur[k - 1])  # (i, j-1)
            Dcur[k] = Ci[k] + m

    jvec = (W - 1) - band + np.arange(K)
    ok_end = (jvec >= 0) & (jvec <= W - 1)
    plen = ((W - 1) + jvec + 2).astype(float)
    Dend = D[W - 1]
    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        normc = np.where(ok_end[:, None], Dend / plen[:, None], inf)
    normc = np.where(np.isfinite(normc), normc, inf)
    kstar = np.argmin(normc, axis=0).astype(np.int64)
    colidx = np.arange(N)
    norm_cost = normc[kstar, colidx]

    s_sum = np.zeros(N)
    s_cnt = np.zeros(N)
    sum_y = np.zeros((W, N))
    cnt_y = np.zeros((W, N))

    i_cur = np.full(N, W - 1, dtype=np.int64)
    k_cur = kstar.copy()
    active = np.isfinite(norm_cost)

    for _ in range(3 * W + 4):
        if not active.any():
            break
        cc = np.flatnonzero(active)
        ic = i_cur[cc]
        kc = k_cur[cc]
        jc = np.clip(ic - band + kc, 0, W - 1)
        off = (band - kc).astype(float)
        s_sum[cc] += np.sign(off)
        s_cnt[cc] += 1.0
        sum_y[ic, cc] += Yraw[jc, cc]
        cnt_y[ic, cc] += 1.0

        at_start = (ic == 0) & (jc == 0)
        ip = np.maximum(ic - 1, 0)
        kp1 = np.minimum(kc + 1, K - 1)
        km1 = np.maximum(kc - 1, 0)
        c_up = np.where((ic > 0) & ((kc + 1) <= (K - 1)), D[ip, kp1, cc], inf)
        c_diag = np.where((ic > 0) & (jc > 0), D[ip, kc, cc], inf)
        c_left = np.where((jc > 0) & ((kc - 1) >= 0), D[ic, km1, cc], inf)
        mbest = np.minimum(c_diag, np.minimum(c_up, c_left))
        fin = np.isfinite(mbest)
        take_diag = fin & (c_diag <= mbest)
        take_up = fin & (~take_diag) & (c_up <= c_left)
        take_left = fin & (~take_diag) & (~take_up)
        new_i = np.where(take_diag | take_up, ic - 1, ic)
        new_k = np.where(take_up, kc + 1, np.where(take_left, kc - 1, kc))
        stop = at_start | (~fin)
        i_cur[cc] = np.where(stop, ic, new_i)
        k_cur[cc] = np.where(stop, kc, new_k)
        active[cc[stop]] = False

    with np.errstate(invalid="ignore", divide="ignore"):
        yhat = sum_y / np.where(cnt_y > 0.0, cnt_y, np.nan)
        s_score = s_sum / np.where(s_cnt > 0.0, s_cnt, np.nan)
    yhat = pd.DataFrame(yhat).ffill().bfill().values
    lag = np.where(np.isfinite(norm_cost), (band - kstar).astype(float), np.nan)
    return s_score, lag, yhat, norm_cost


@register_factor
class VLGrangerDTWBacklogCatchup(BaseFactor):
    """Band-limited DTW alignment of a stock's path to its sector leader path; long the not-yet-emulated leader backlog."""

    factor_id = "vl_granger_dtw_backlog_catchup"
    name = "Variable-Lag DTW Alignment Backlog Catch-Up"
    category = "statistical_arbitrage"
    description = (
        "Rolling band-limited DTW between each name's volatility-normalised "
        "cumulative log-price path and the volume-weighted cumulative path of its "
        "sector peers (self excluded).  Retains the warp-offset sign score s(P), "
        "the endpoint (variable) lag, the emulation gain beta from regressing "
        "follower increments on the warp-reconstructed leader increments, and a "
        "variable-lag vs own-past / best-fixed-lag residual-variance gate.  Signal "
        "= beta * leader cumulative return over the last endpoint-lag bars, gated "
        "and sector-demeaned, then cross-sectionally ranked."
    )
    window_length = 320
    inputs = ["close", "volume", "sector"]
    prediction_horizon = 6
    suggested_horizons = [6]

    _WIN = 180          # DTW window length in bars
    _BAND = 12          # Sakoe-Chiba half width (delta_max) in bars
    _MAX_EVALS = 300    # throttle on the number of DTW re-estimations

    def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
        close = data["close"].astype(float)
        volume = data["volume"].astype(float).abs()
        out = pd.DataFrame(0.0, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)

        T, N = close.shape
        W = int(self._WIN)
        band = int(self._BAND)
        if T < W + 8 or N < 4:
            return out

        # ---- static sector labels (first observed value per name) ------------
        sector = data.get("sector")
        labels = {}
        if isinstance(sector, pd.DataFrame):
            sec = sector.reindex(columns=close.columns)
            for c in close.columns:
                col = sec[c].dropna()
                labels[c] = str(col.iloc[0]) if len(col) else "UNKNOWN"
        else:
            for c in close.columns:
                labels[c] = "UNKNOWN"
        groups = defaultdict(list)
        for c in close.columns:
            groups[labels[c]].append(c)

        col_pos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(close.columns)}
        group_ok = np.zeros(N, dtype=bool)
        for lab, cols in groups.items():
            if len(cols) >= 4:
                for c in cols:
                    group_ok[col_pos[c]] = True
        if not group_ok.any():
            return out

        # ---- follower and leader increment panels ---------------------------
        px = close.where(close > 0.0)
        r = np.log(px).diff()
        dvol = (px * volume).rolling(120, min_periods=20).mean()
        wgt = dvol.where(dvol > 0.0)

        lead = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=close.index, columns=close.columns)
        for lab, cols in groups.items():
            if len(cols) < 4:
                continue
            sub_r = r[cols]
            sub_w = wgt[cols].where(sub_r.notna(), 0.0).fillna(0.0)
            sub_r0 = sub_r.fillna(0.0)
            wr = sub_r0 * sub_w
            num = wr.sum(axis=1)
            den = sub_w.sum(axis=1)
            numer = (-wr).add(num, axis=0)
            denom = (-sub_w).add(den, axis=0).replace(0.0, np.nan)
            lead[cols] = numer / denom

        rv = r.values
        lrv = lead.values

        beta_arr = np.full((T, N), np.nan)
        lag_arr = np.full((T, N), np.nan)
        gate_arr = np.full((T, N), np.nan)

        step = max(30, int(math.ceil(float(T) / float(self._MAX_EVALS))))
        eval_idx = list(range(W - 1, T, step))
        if not eval_idx:
            return out
        if eval_idx[-1] != T - 1:
            eval_idx.append(T - 1)

        min_obs = 0.75 * W

        for t in eval_idx:
            rx = rv[t - W + 1:t + 1, :]
            ry = lrv[t - W + 1:t + 1, :]
            fin_x = np.isfinite(rx)
            fin_y = np.isfinite(ry)
            rxc = np.where(fin_x, rx, 0.0)
            ryc = np.where(fin_y, ry, 0.0)
            sx = rxc.std(0)
            sy = ryc.std(0)
            valid = (
                group_ok
                & (fin_x.sum(0) >= min_obs)
                & (fin_y.sum(0) >= min_obs)
                & (sx > 0.0)
                & (sy > 0.0)
            )
            sel = np.flatnonzero(valid)
            if sel.size < 2:
                continue

            rx_s = rxc[:, sel]
            ry_s = ryc[:, sel]
            Xraw = np.cumsum(rx_s, axis=0)
            Yraw = np.cumsum(ry_s, axis=0)
            scale_x = sx[sel] * math.sqrt(float(W))
            scale_y = sy[sel] * math.sqrt(float(W))
            Xn = Xraw / scale_x
            Yn = Yraw / scale_y

            s_score, lag, yhat, norm_cost = _banded_dtw_panel(Xn, Yn, Yraw, band)

            # ---- variable-lag vs fixed-lag residual comparison --------------
            dx = rx_s[1:, :]
            dy = ry_s[1:, :]
            dyh = np.diff(yhat, axis=0)
            M = dx.shape[0]
            if M <= band + 8:
                continue
            y_dep = dx[band:, :]
            x_own = dx[band - 1:M - 1, :]
            x_vl = dyh[band:, :]
            resid_vl, beta = _ols2_resid_var(y_dep, x_own, x_vl)
            resid_own = _ols1_resid_var(y_dep, x_own)
            resid_fix = np.full(sel.size, np.inf)
            for l in range(1, band + 1):
                xl = dy[band - l:M - l, :]
                rvar, _ = _ols2_resid_var(y_dep, x_own, xl)
                rvar = np.where(np.isfinite(rvar), rvar, np.inf)
                resid_fix = np.minimum(resid_fix, rvar)

            beta = np.where(np.isfinite(beta), beta, np.nan)
            beta = np.clip(beta, -5.0, 5.0)

            finite_cost = np.isfinite(norm_cost)
            if finite_cost.any():
                med_cost = float(np.median(norm_cost[finite_cost]))
            else:
                med_cost = np.nan
            with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
                sim_gate = finite_cost & (norm_cost <= med_cost)
                vl_gate = (
                    np.isfinite(resid_vl)
                    & (resid_vl < resid_own)
                    & (resid_vl < resid_fix)
                )
                gate = (
                    sim_gate
                    & vl_gate
                    & (np.nan_to_num(s_score, nan=-1.0) > 0.05)
                    & (np.nan_to_num(lag, nan=-1.0) >= 1.0)
                    & (np.nan_to_num(beta, nan=-1.0) > 0.0)
                )

            beta_arr[t, sel] = np.nan_to_num(beta, nan=0.0)
            lag_arr[t, sel] = np.nan_to_num(lag, nan=0.0)
            gate_arr[t, sel] = np.where(gate, 1.0, 0.0)

        idx = close.index
        cols = close.columns
        beta_df = pd.DataFrame(beta_arr, index=idx, columns=cols).ffill(limit=int(step))
        lag_df = pd.DataFrame(lag_arr, index=idx, columns=cols).ffill(limit=int(step))
        gate_df = pd.DataFrame(gate_arr, index=idx, columns=cols).ffill(limit=int(step))

        # ---- per-bar backlog: leader move over the last Delta_T bars --------
        Lv = np.cumsum(np.nan_to_num(lrv, nan=0.0, posinf=0.0, neginf=0.0), axis=0)
        lagv = lag_df.values
        lag_i = np.where(np.isfinite(lagv), lagv, 0.0)
        lag_i = np.clip(lag_i, 0.0, float(band)).astype(np.int64)
        rows = np.arange(T, dtype=np.int64)[:, None] - lag_i
        rows = np.clip(rows, 0, T - 1)
        back = Lv - np.take_along_axis(Lv, rows, 0)
        back_df = pd.DataFrame(back, index=idx, columns=cols)

        raw = beta_df * back_df
        raw = raw.where(gate_df > 0.5)
        raw = raw.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan)

        # ---- sector demean, then cross-sectional rank -----------------------
        dem = pd.DataFrame(np.nan, index=idx, columns=cols)
        for lab, gcols in groups.items():
            if len(gcols) < 4:
                continue
            sub = raw[gcols]
            dem[gcols] = sub.sub(sub.mean(axis=1), axis=0)

        sig = rank(dem) - 0.5
        sig = sig.replace([np.inf, -np.inf], np.nan).fillna(0.0)
        return sig.reindex(index=idx, columns=cols).fillna(0.0)

    import pandas as pd

    from quant_fund_agent.factors.base import BaseFactor
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.ops import rank, returns
    from quant_fund_agent.factors.registry import register_factor


    def _variance_ratio(ret: pd.DataFrame, k: int, n: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
        """Lo–MacKinlay variance ratio over horizon k, estimated on a trailing
        n-bar window.  VR < 1 => mean-reverting, VR > 1 => trending.  Causal:
        every term is a trailing rolling statistic, so value at t sees only <= t."""
        var_1 = ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        k_ret = ret.rolling(k, min_periods=k).sum()          # overlapping k-bar returns
        var_k = k_ret.rolling(n, min_periods=n).var()
        return var_k / (k * var_1).replace(0.0, np.nan)


    @register_factor
    class VarianceRatioReversion(BaseFactor):
        factor_id = "variance_ratio_reversion"
        name = "Variance-ratio reversion"
        category = "mean_reversion"
        description = (
            "Cross-sectional rank of (1 - trailing variance ratio): long the "
            "most mean-reverting names, short the most trending ones."
        )
        window_length = 120
        inputs = ["close"]
        prediction_horizon = 12
        suggested_horizons = [6, 12, 24]

        def calc(self, data: dict[str, pd.DataFrame]) -> pd.DataFrame:
            ret = returns(data)
            vr = _variance_ratio(ret, 5, 100)
            return rank(1.0 - vr)
